subject: Private VPC connectivity orchestration — allowlist, PrivateLink vs Peering, owner matrix
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@alphainsights.com>, Procurement <procurement@alphainsights.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Private VPC connectivity orchestration — allowlist, PrivateLink vs Peering, owner matrix

Elena / team,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the clear signal around the data residency and network controls needed for Alpha Insights. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a networking kickoff on the calendar: 

Call recap (high level)
- Primary requirement: customer-managed private connectivity (no public egress from model payloads).
- Preference: Private VPC (PrivateLink or peering) for production, while Hosted API OK for short-term evals.
- Procurement: vendor questionnaire and standard SOW questions are in flight (procurement on copy).

Recommended paths we discussed
- Hosted API: fastest to validate models, but not acceptable for production due to policy.
- Redwood Dedicated: reserved GPU pools in our tenancy; still requires network egress model discussion.
- Private VPC (recommended for prod): two architecture options — AWS PrivateLink (endpoint service) or VPC Peering (cross-account). PrivateLink usually reduces blast radius and is easier for allowlist enforcement; peering can be simpler in some orgs but requires route management.

Network items we need from Alpha (ask list)
1) Network owner + best contact for a short tech kickoff (L3/L4 network engineer).
2) Desired timeline for production cutover (target week or month).
3) CIDR(s) for the consumer VPC(s) and whether you can accept endpoint service (PrivateLink) or prefer peering.
4) Firewall / ACL team owner who will manage the egress allowlist.
5) Any constrained egress IP policy (we can provide static egress IP ranges if you need a small allowlist).

Redwood deliverables (next)
- I will create a short owner matrix and proposed owners for each task. Ben will produce a minimal egress IP list we can publish for allowlists.
- Kimberly will draft a PrivateLink vs Peering pros/cons doc tailored to Alpha's constraints.
- I will schedule a 45-min network kickoff once you provide the network owner.

Attachments: alpha_connectivity_checklist.xlsx (fillable checklist), redwood-vpc-options.pdf (architecture summary).

Proposed owners (initial):
- Redwood network lead: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.com)
- Redwood solution architect: Kimberly Park (kimberly.park@redwood.com)
- Alpha network owner: (TBD)

Next steps / asks for Elena: please reply with the network owner + 2 windows next week for a kickoff. If procurement has any gating items I should loop in, flag them here and I'll coordinate with our legal/finance contacts.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private VPC connectivity orchestration — allowlist, PrivateLink vs Peering, owner matrix

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and the checklist, very helpful. A few clarifying Qs from our side before I loop in our network owner: 

1) Can Redwood host the peering/endpoint on your side (i.e., do you create the endpoint service) or do we need to provision the peering from our account first?
2) If we go PrivateLink, can you provide a single static egress IP range we can add to our central allowlist (we manage a centralized egress policy across multiple projects)?
3) Do you have any hard requirements on source CIDR size or subnetting on our side for peering/endpoint?

Timeline: procurement would like to target the first half of July for production readiness; we need the technical kickoff this week or next to meet that schedule.

Network owner: I will confirm the right network contact in an hour (likely Rafael in Network Ops). Procurement is on copy for contract-specific items.

Attachments: redwood_private_link_one-pager.pdf (for our internal security team).

—Elena
Elena Morales
VP, Platform Engineering
Alpha Insights

Subject: Re: Private VPC connectivity orchestration — allowlist, PrivateLink vs Peering, owner matrix

Elena — great, thanks. Quick answers and a concrete next-step plan below.

Q&A
- Peering/endpoint provisioning: Redwood can stand up an endpoint service (PrivateLink) from our account and provide the service name for you to create the endpoint on your side. For peering, alpha will need to request peering from your account and accept on our side — both models are supported.
- Static egress IPs: Yes — Ben will publish a minimal set of static egress IP ranges we can commit to for allowlisting. Those will be NAT egress IPs from the Private deployment path.
- CIDR/subnet constraints: No hard requirements beyond usual AWS guidance; we prefer non-overlapping CIDRs. If you share your consumer CIDRs we will validate routing.

Proposed immediate plan
1) Network kickoff (45m): agenda to cover endpoint vs peering decision, egress IPs, firewall rules, and timeline.
   - Proposed windows: 2027-05-26 09:00-09:45 PT or 2027-05-27 11:00-11:45 PT.
2) Ben to send egress IP proposal by 2027-05-25 EOD.
3) Kimberly to circulate a 1-pager comparing PrivateLink vs Peering specific to Alpha's constraints by 2027-05-25 EOD.

Owners (confirmed):
- Redwood: Ben Carter — network lead (ben.carter@redwood.com)
- Redwood: Kimberly Park — solution architecture (kimberly.park@redwood.com)
- Alpha: Rafael (Network Ops) — please confirm role and email when you have it.

HubSpot / procurement notes: deal ID ALPHA-2027-001; procurement please advise if we should start drafting the SOW now or wait until network model is decided. HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/view/67890
